page: Microsoft Azure E128-32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Edsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, containing 16 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. It includes 7559 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, with no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in specific memory and compression tasks. The server achieved a strong rating in memory bandwidth for large-block read-only (238.84 GB/sec) and write (137.13 GB/sec) operations, alongside a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.18 GB/sec. Passmark CPU physics testing also registered in the top 25% tier at 7302.83. Other metrics, including stress-ng single-core (1947.98) and multi-core (31881.31) CPU performance, Passmark database operations (18851.38), and Redis SET operations (43.41 million operations/sec), align with average tier performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E128-32ds_v6 offers high resource density, particularly for memory-bound workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. The combination of 1024.0 GB of RAM and 7559 GB of local storage makes it suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, data warehousing, and enterprise applications requiring substantial local scratch space.

Benchmark results show strong performance in large-block memory bandwidth, with read-only speeds of 238.84 GB/sec and write speeds of 137.13 GB/sec, as well as a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.18 GB/sec. CPU and database benchmarks, such as Redis SET operations at 43.41 million operations per second, perform in the average tier. This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale databases, and data warehousing applications requiring substantial local storage capacity without GPU acceleration.
